name: Independent cryptic crossword, Penguin book 1 No 9

book.title: The Penguin Book of Independent Crosswords, volume 1

clue.text: Raced around the outer edge and skidded

indicators.note: one word going around another wraps it, so the second sits inside the first

blocks.note: raced means went fast
a lip is the rim or outer edge of a vessel

explanation.surface: A racing driver tears round the outside of the track and loses grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outer edge' sounds like the track's boundary, but it is just a rim.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip is to lose footing or grip and slide, the same as a skid.

clue.text: A High Church feature

blocks.note: surface reading: the Anglo-Catholic wing of the Church of England and its rituals
setter's reading: the tallest part of a church building, rising to a point

explanation.walkthrough: High Church is a style of worship; read literally it is the high part of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is the tall tower topped by a spire on a church building.

clue.text: Forward about five, though extremely hard-up

indicators.note: about means round, so the word for forward wraps the numeral

blocks.note: forward means cheeky or impudent
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A cheeky person with five kids is still broke.
explanation.walkthrough: V goes inside INSOLENT. 'Extremely' looks like it trims a word's ends, but it simply intensifies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insolvent cannot pay debts, which is being badly short of money.

clue.text: There's very little here to steal

blocks.note: first meaning: a tiny amount, such as one held between finger and thumb
second meaning: to nick or filch, informal

explanation.surface: A burglar finds a house with nothing worth taking.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinch of salt is a minute quantity, and to pinch is slang for to steal.

clue.text: Blunt expression of anti-Thatcherism?

blocks.note: first meaning: frank, straightforward, plain-spoken
second meaning, punning: a slogan wishing the political right defeated, 'Down with the right!'

explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher led Britain's Conservative government in the 1980s, the political right; a protester against her might cry 'Down, Right!'
explanation.definitionFit: Downright as an adjective means thoroughly frank or plain-spoken, outspoken without softening.

clue.text: Nurse having aspiration after riches possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several possible arrangements of the letters
after sends the aspiration piece to the end, behind the rearranged word

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
aspiration is the breathy H sound

explanation.surface: Someone cherishes a hope of wealth, with greed hinted at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the H behind the rearranged letters. In grammar an aspirate is an H sound, so aspiration gives H.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a hope or grudge is to hold it dearly and foster it, which is to cherish it.

clue.text: Get over feeling angry

blocks.note: first meaning: to go across a road or river
second meaning: annoyed or irritated

explanation.surface: Advice to someone to put their temper behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross a road is to get over to the other side; a cross person is annoyed.

clue.text: They're responsible for the leavings

blocks.note: surface reading: leftovers, scraps from a meal that someone must clear up
setter's reading: what the dead leave behind them in a will

explanation.walkthrough: Leavings sounds like food scraps but means a dead person's bequests.
explanation.definitionFit: Executors are the people named in a will to carry out its terms and distribute the estate.

clue.text: A figure at first thought perfect

indicators.note: at first tells us the next item comes before, not after, the earlier piece

blocks.note: an idea is a thought
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: A shape that seemed flawless on first impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' puts IDEA ahead of L. 'A figure' suggests a body shape but is a number here.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means perfect, the best that could be imagined.

clue.text: The case for a gun woman carrying assorted lots

indicators.note: assorted means mixed up, so the letters are jumbled
carrying means holding within, so the woman word goes round the jumbled letters

blocks.note: her refers to a woman
taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman lugging various items makes the argument for owning a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The case for' looks like an argument in favour; it is a literal gun case.
explanation.definitionFit: A holster is a leather sheath worn on a belt or under the arm to hold a pistol.

clue.text: A couple of letters for a place in Germany

blocks.note: the names of two letters of the alphabet, ESS and EN, spelt out in full

explanation.surface: A couple of letters are posted to an address in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are S and N written as words: ESS + EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of western Germany.

clue.text: Not the kind of bread for making a sandwich!

definitions.text: Not the kind of bread for making a sandwich!

blocks.clueFragment: Not the kind of bread for making a sandwich!
blocks.note: surface reading: a type of loaf unsuited to sandwiches
setter's reading: a sandwich is a snack, not a complete full dinner, yet the bread's name says otherwise

explanation.walkthrough: The bread's name splits as WHOLE MEAL, and a sandwich is a snack rather than an entire meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholemeal bread is made from flour that keeps the entire grain, bran included.

clue.text: Fish and a vegetable taken in error returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the error word is read right to left
taken in means swallowed up, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a slip is a small mistake
chard is a leafy green vegetable

explanation.surface: A cook regrets serving fish with the wrong vegetable and sends it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' reads as sending the dish back but applies only to the word for error.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilchards are small oily sea fish of the herring family, often sold tinned.

clue.text: One gets left inside in the dark

indicators.note: one gets something when receiving it, so the first piece takes the other into itself
inside places the left letter within the word for one

blocks.note: a unit is a single thing, one
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone is abandoned indoors with the lights off.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside UNIT to make UN-L-IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlit has no lamp or light switched on, so it lies dark; the phrase works as an adjective.

clue.text: Leave of absence, formerly to dine

blocks.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone once got time off to go out for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: EXEAT is Latin for 'let him go out'.
explanation.definitionFit: An exeat is permission granted by a school or college for a student to be away for a period.

clue.text: The point about indignation when fruit is served

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the point word wraps the indignation word

blocks.note: a tine is the prong or point of a fork
indignation is righteous anger

explanation.surface: A diner is outraged when the fruit course arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: A tine is one prong of a fork, so 'the point' fits the dining scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small, loose-skinned orange citrus fruit like a mandarin.

clue.text: Fuel store cut by senior

blocks.note: a gash is a deep cut
senior means older in age

explanation.surface: An elderly official reduces the fuel supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut by' looks like a verb acting on the store, but the two words just sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasholder is the large telescoping tank that held town gas for domestic supply.

clue.text: Alert agent receiving exact money

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the agent word holds the other pieces

blocks.note: a spy is a secret agent
right means correct or exact
L is the symbol for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A sharp secret agent is paid the precise sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exact money' looks like a single phrase about change but splits in two; L for pound comes from the Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly means lively and full of energy, quick and on the ball.

clue.text: Essential if one is to get a bite

definitions.text: Essential if one is to get a bite

blocks.note: surface reading: an angler hoping for fish to take the bait, or a hungry person after a snack

blocks.clueFragment: Essential if one is to get a bite
blocks.note: setter's reading: the set of teeth needed to bite anything at all

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get a bite' suggests fishing; it is literally biting, which needs teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentation is the arrangement of teeth, or toothed edging, in an animal or on a leaf.

clue.text: Not read to — may well get explosive!

indicators.note: may well get suggests the words could turn into something else when rearranged

blocks.note: the three words taken as letters to shuffle

explanation.surface: A child who misses a bedtime story is likely to throw a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue's ending: a device that sets off a blast, making things explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is the small device that triggers a charge, so with it a bomb becomes live.

clue.text: Expiry at the end of the year still

blocks.note: December is the last month of the year, abbreviated DEC
to still pain is to ease it

explanation.surface: Something expires, unmoving, as December closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb but is the verb meaning calm or soothe.
explanation.definitionFit: Decease is a formal word for death, the end of a person's life.

clue.text: Dawn sees a French male in drink

indicators.note: in puts the French word inside the word for drink

blocks.note: to sup is to drink in sips
un is the masculine form of 'a' in French

explanation.surface: At daybreak a Frenchman is found in his cups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A French male' is not a man but the masculine form of the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunup is the moment the sun rises above the horizon, the start of daybreak.

clue.text: Parking soldiers are apt to claim

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to tend to do something is to be apt or inclined to do it

explanation.surface: Soldiers tend to say they are allowed to park.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend in an older sense is to assert or lay claim, as a pretender claims a throne.

clue.text: Petition causing many to talk wildly

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
to rave is to speak incoherently or wildly

explanation.surface: A petition stirs up a crowd into ranting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' giving C (100) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To crave is an old sense meaning to beg earnestly or ask humbly for something.

clue.text: Asia's composers appear very musical

indicators.note: composers put pieces together, so these letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: the word taken as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Asian composers prove to be highly musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composers' looks like the subject, musicians; it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is an Italian term in musical directions meaning very, as in allegro assai.

clue.text: Decree member is procrastinatory

blocks.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
taken as written
putting things off makes one tardy

explanation.surface: A slow-moving member of parliament delays passing a decree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a politician but means a limb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make laws, to enact by formal ruling.

clue.text: Allow about a quarter — that's the minimum

indicators.note: about means around, so the allow word goes around the others

blocks.note: to let is to allow
taken as written
south is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Budget a quarter of the amount, and no less.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass points are called quarters, so a quarter can be N, S, E or W.
explanation.definitionFit: The least is the smallest possible amount, which is the minimum.

clue.text: It's apparently good in water colour

indicators.note: in puts the good word within the water word

blocks.note: the sea is a body of water
pi is short for pious, good

explanation.surface: Something seems to work well as a watercolour paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water colour' looks like one word for a painting; it splits into wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown pigment and tint, originally made from cuttlefish ink.

clue.text: He'll be aggressive when put out by a worker

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
a ship puts out to sea when it sets sail
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker; by means next to

explanation.surface: Someone turns nasty after being sacked by a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' suggests annoyed; here it is a ship leaving harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is an attacker, one who acts with violence against another person.

clue.text: Force up value, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its sound, not spelling

blocks.note: a price is the value set on something

explanation.surface: Prices are being pushed up, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: To prise something is to lever it open or up using force.

clue.text: The famous — some of them in entertainment

indicators.note: some of means only a part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word, a whole word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Celebrities make up part of the world of show business.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in thEM IN ENTertainment. The definition is plural-sounding, but 'the famous' works as an adjective phrase too.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent people are distinguished, celebrated and well known in their field.

clue.text: Told tales about the Orient and felt a great longing for it

definitions.text: felt a great longing for it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for told tales goes around the other

blocks.note: to yarn is to tell long stories
the Orient is the East, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A traveller spins stories of the East and longs to go back.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside YARNED after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long intensely for something; 'for it' is part of the sense of longing.
